headline: Your work is making news. Your website should look like it.
intro: From the Twitty Park lawsuit to Georgia's first Superfund Research Center, 2026 has been a big year for GEC. Your content is current and your calendar is full, but the design hasn't kept up, and your team is writing every post by hand. Here's a plan for both: a fresh, modern look on the Wix site you already have, and AI tools that turn each announcement into ready-to-review posts.
working: An up-to-date events calendar with RSVP links
Press releases and news coverage posted regularly
Clear ways to act: report air problems, donate, volunteer
Named staff and board, and a story that goes back to 1990

findings.title: The design hasn't kept up with the work.
findings.detail: The homepage leans on menus and blocks of text, with few visuals to explain six program areas at a glance. Simple illustrations and icons would make the site feel as current as your news.

findings.title: Small details undercut a strong site.
findings.detail: The About Us page lists a "Seafood Outreach Assitant," and the LinkedIn icon on every page has no link.

findings.title: Big news arrives in bursts.
findings.detail: Nine of this year's 13 news items came out in a single week in June, around the Superfund Research Center announcement. Each one could have become a week of posts, a newsletter story and an explainer.

findings.title: The Superfund page doesn't name the sites.
findings.detail: It says Glynn County is home to 4 of Georgia's 16 Superfund sites, but doesn't name them or link to any reports, just as the new research center is drawing attention to them.

findings.title: Technical topics need plain language.
findings.detail: Air quality, seafood safety and Superfund cleanups come with dense EPA and EPD documents. AI tools can draft plain-language summaries for your team to check, so more residents understand what's at stake.

outcome: A refreshed Wix site with a modern design, custom coastal illustrations and icons for each program, a Superfund page that names the sites, and every typo and dead link fixed. Plus two AI tools and a one-hour training: one turns each press release into ready-to-review posts and a newsletter story, the other drafts plain-language explainers. Your team reviews everything before it's published.
timeline: About 3 weeks from kickoff to launch, including the AI training session.

package.note: A new design for your current Wix site: homepage, program pages and About Us, custom illustrations and program icons, a Superfund page that names each site, and every typo and dead link fixed. Your team keeps editing in Wix.
A press-release-to-posts assistant and a plain-language explainer assistant, set up with your voice, your facts and your review steps, plus a 1-hour team training and a written how-to guide.

addons.note: I write and schedule 8 posts a month on 2 platforms from your news and events, so your team only has to approve them.
Make sure your Google listing, Facebook and Instagram all share the same up-to-date information and links.
